With cheese and butter.
Kuymak (mıhlama, cheesy cornmeal)
2 tablespoons cornmeal
150 g çeçil or string cheese
Melt the butter.
Toast the cornmeal for 2 minutes.
Add the water and stir.
Add the cheese and cook until stretchy.
The cheese is salty, so don’t add salt.
Oven-baked granola
3 cups oats
1 cup mixed nuts
Half a cup raisins
Preheat the oven to 160 °C.
Mix the oats, nuts and cinnamon.
Add the honey and oil and toss.
Spread on a tray and bake for 25 minutes, stirring twice.
Add the raisins once cool.
It crisps up as it cools.
With yogurt or milk.
2 weeks in a jar.
Cheesy potato rösti
Grate the potatoes and squeeze out the liquid thoroughly.
Mix with the egg, kashar and salt.
Drop into oil as flat patties.
Fry for 5 minutes on each side.
Well-squeezed potatoes turn out crisp.
Kazandibi (pan-made)
2 tablespoons icing sugar for the base
Whisk the milk, sugar, flours and starch while cold and cook, stirring, until boiling.
Once thickened, add the vanilla and butter.
Sprinkle a thin layer of icing sugar in the pan and caramelise over medium heat.
Pour the pudding into the pan and burn the base for 5–6 minutes.
Let cool and cut into rolls.
While burning the base, take off the heat as soon as you smell it at the edges.
Keşkül (almond pudding)
1 cup almond flour
2 tablespoons coconut and 2 tablespoons pistachios
Bring the milk, sugar and almond flour to the boil.
Loosen the rice flour and egg yolk with a little milk and add.
Add the vanilla.
Pour into bowls, chill and decorate.
Almond flour gives keşkül an intense aroma.
Supangle (chocolate pudding)
100 g dark chocolate
Whisk the milk, sugar, cocoa, flour and starch.
Bring to the boil, stirring constantly.
Once thickened, add the chocolate and butter.
Pour into bowls.
Chill and serve with grated chocolate.
You can put biscuits in the bowl as a base.
Aşure (Noah’s pudding)
1 cup hulled wheat for aşure
Half a cup chickpeas and half a cup haricot beans (boiled)
10 dried apricots, 10 dried figs
1 orange peel
Half a cup walnuts, 3 tablespoons pomegranate seeds, 1 teaspoon cinnamon
Soak the wheat overnight and cook with 8 glasses of water for 1 hour.
Add the chickpeas, beans and chopped dried fruit.
Add the sugar and orange peel and cook for 45 minutes.
Divide between bowls and let cool.
Decorate with walnuts, pomegranate and cinnamon.
Aşure thickens as it cools.
5 days in the fridge.
Profiteroles
Cream: 2 cups milk, 3 tablespoons sugar, 2 tablespoons cornflour
Sauce: 150 g dark chocolate, half a cup milk
Bring the water and butter to the boil, add the flour and stir until the dough comes together.
Once cool, beat in the eggs one at a time.
Pipe walnut-sized mounds and bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes (don’t open the door for the first 15 minutes).
Cook and cool the cream, then fill the pastries.
Pour the melted chocolate sauce over the top.
Opening the oven door too early makes the pastry collapse.
Tiramisu (egg-free)
250 g mascarpone or labneh
1 packet ladyfinger biscuits
1 cup cold coffee
Whip the cream with icing sugar, add the mascarpone and mix.
Dip the biscuits quickly in the coffee and arrange in a dish.
Spread half the cream.
Make another layer of biscuits and cream.
Chill for at least 4 hours and dust with cocoa.
Don’t leave the biscuits in the coffee or they fall apart.
Apple pie
250 g butter
Filling: 5 apples, half a cup sugar, 1 dessert spoon cinnamon, half a cup walnuts
Make a dough with the butter, icing sugar, egg and flour; rest for 30 minutes.
Press two-thirds of the dough into a tart tin and add the filling.
Make a lattice with the remaining dough.
Bake at 180 °C for 40 minutes.
Keep the dough cold so it rolls out easily.
Cheesecake (baked)
200 g oat biscuits
80 g melted butter
600 g labneh
Zest of 1 lemon
Crumble the biscuits, mix with the butter and press into the base of the tin.
Beat the labneh and sugar; add the eggs one at a time.
Add the cream, flour and lemon zest.
Bake at 170 °C for 60 minutes; let cool in the oven with the door ajar.
Chill for at least 6 hours.
Cooling slowly prevents the surface cracking.
Cold, with fruit sauce.
Trileçe (three-milk cake)
Milk mixture: 1 cup milk, half a cup cream, 3 tablespoons sugar
Caramel: 4 tablespoons sugar, half a cup cream
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 5 minutes until frothy, then add the flour and baking powder.
Bake the cake batter at 180 °C for 30 minutes.
Pour the milk mixture over the lukewarm cake and let it soak in.
Caramelise the sugar and add the cream to make a sauce.
Spread the sauce over the top and chill.
Pour on the milk before the cake has cooled completely.
Güllaç (rose-milk wafer dessert)
10 güllaç sheets
1.5 litres milk
1 dessert spoon rose water
1 cup walnuts
Warm the milk and sugar until lukewarm and add the rose water.
